findings.title: Sanitize HTML even when bypassing Markdown rendering
findings.body: The new raw_html mode returns raw content without sanitization. PollFeed passes external feed content into this mode through TopicEmbed.import, and Nokogiri parsing only rewrites URLs—it preserves scripts, event handlers, and unsafe link schemes. For example, an imported image with an onerror handler becomes executable stored HTML in the forum's origin. Edits to these posts retain the same bypass. Keep an HTML sanitization step on every cook.

findings.title: Remove the incomplete postfix condition from the closing tag
findings.body: This tag emits `end if` without a condition instead of closing the block with `end`. The incomplete Ruby statement breaks compilation of the ERB template, so requests for URLs with an existing TopicEmbed fail when rendering the discussion. The controller specs do not render views and therefore do not catch this.

findings.title: Validate redirect destinations before fetching them
findings.body: TopicRetriever checks the initial URL's hostname, but open-uri follows redirects here without rechecking the destination. An allowed-host URL that redirects to another host, including an internal HTTP service, bypasses the embed-host allowlist; the server fetches that response and may publish its content as the configured import user. Validate each redirect target before issuing the next request rather than following redirects unchecked.

findings.title: Handle RSS description fields and entries without content
findings.body: Valid RSS items commonly provide their body through description or content:encoded rather than the Atom content field; Atom entries can also contain only summary. For those entries, i.content is nil and calling scrub raises NoMethodError, aborting the entire feed import. Select the available body field and handle missing content explicitly. The current specs only test whether poll_feed is called, not whether a real feed can be imported.

findings.title: Resolve relative references using the source URL
findings.body: The string concatenation mishandles standard URL references. For an article at https://blog.example/posts/one, src='//cdn.example/image.png' becomes https://blog.example/cdn.example/image.png, while href='two.html' is left unchanged and resolves against the forum instead of the source article. Both links and images can therefore break after import. Resolve references against the complete source URI rather than stripping leading slashes and prepending the host.

findings.title: Defer post-creation jobs until the outer transaction commits
findings.body: PostCreator.create enqueues process_post and feature_topic_users before returning. Wrapping it in this additional Topic.transaction means those jobs are now published while the new topic and post remain uncommitted. A fast worker can execute them before their records are visible, causing processing to fail or be skipped; a subsequent rollback also leaves jobs for nonexistent records. Preserve the atomic import but defer job publication until the enclosing transaction commits.

findings.title: Set the retrieval marker and its expiry atomically
findings.body: SETNX and EXPIRE are separate operations. If the worker exits after SETNX succeeds but before EXPIRE runs, the marker remains indefinitely and retrieved_recently? suppresses every subsequent retrieval of that URL. Without feed polling, the embed stays on the loading page permanently despite repeated requests. Create the marker with its expiry in one atomic Redis operation.

findings.title: Preserve exported thread timestamps during Disqus imports
findings.body: The previous PostCreator call supplied the exported thread's created_at value. TopicEmbed.import_remote does not forward a creation timestamp, so historical topics and their first posts are now dated at import time while their replies still use the original exported dates. This corrupts discussion chronology and makes old threads appear newly created. Pass the thread timestamp through the new import API.

findings.title: Compare postMessage origins exactly
findings.body: A substring check accepts origins that are merely prefixes of the configured origin. For example, discourseUrl='https://forum.example.com/' accepts a message from 'https://forum.example.co'. A window on that different domain with a reference to the embedding page can send resize messages to hide or stretch the comments iframe. Compare against the parsed, exact Discourse origin and verify that e.source is the iframe's contentWindow.
